sections.title: What This Module Covers
sections.body: This module covers building RESTful JSON APIs with Rails — the most common use case for Rails in modern backend development. You will learn: the RESTful routing conventions (resources :posts generates 7 routes mapped to standard HTTP verb + path combinations), rendering JSON responses with render json:, the HTTP verbs and their semantics (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE), the HTTP status codes that APIs use (200, 201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 422, 500) and when to use each, the full request-response cycle in a Rails API context, and the difference between a full-stack Rails app (ActionController::Base) and a Rails API-only app (ActionController::API).

sections.title: Key Concepts at a Glance
sections.body: RESTful routes: GET /posts => index, GET /posts/:id => show, POST /posts => create, PATCH /posts/:id => update, DELETE /posts/:id => destroy. Rendering JSON: render json: @post (calls to_json). render json: @post, status: :created (201). render json: { error: 'Not found' }, status: :not_found (404). HTTP verbs: GET (read, idempotent), POST (create), PUT (replace entire resource), PATCH (partial update), DELETE (remove). Status codes: 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized (not authenticated), 403 Forbidden (authenticated but not allowed), 404 Not Found, 422 Unprocessable Entity (validation failed), 500 Internal Server Error. API mode: rails new app --api omits cookies, sessions, view layer. Inherits from ActionController::API instead of Base. respond_to :json at class level. before_action for authentication checks. rescue_from for consistent error JSON.

sections.title: What Interviewers Ask Freshers
sections.body: Key API fresher questions: (1) What is REST? Name the constraints. (2) What are the differences between PUT and PATCH? (3) What status code should you return when creating a resource successfully? (4) What is the difference between 401 and 403? (5) What does resources :posts generate in routes? (6) How do you return a JSON response in a Rails controller? (7) What is the difference between a full Rails app and a Rails API-only app? (8) What happens during the request-response cycle in a Rails API? (9) What status code should you return when a validation fails? (10) How would you structure a versioned API in Rails (e.g., /api/v1/posts)? These questions assess your understanding of how modern Rails is used in production.
